text:
maria-ops: seeing a weird spike from ORD POP starting ~08:10 UTC, p99 up ~320ms -> 780ms, throughput dropped ~22% across a subset of hosts. KV cache hit-rate dipped at same time.

alex_k: saw the alert. any recent deploys?

deploy-bot: deploy completed by sasha at 08:05 UTC to service=runtime-ord, revision=2026.03.16-7a9c

sasha: yes pushed a small batching tweak (adaptive window change) and a kernel-selector tweak before the window. didn't expect this large of a regression.

maria-ops: the pattern looks like short bursts of packet loss to the upstream peering (isp hutch -> backbone). RTT jitter increased and we saw retransmits, which correlates with KV cache warming/thrashing.

alex_k: log tail from one affected host:
```
[08:09:58] kvcache: eviction threshold crossed, evicting 14 entries
[08:09:59] batcher: flush due to max-latency=200ms, queued=18
[08:10:00] net: retransmit detected for 10 flows to 13.52.0.0/16 via next-hop 198.51.100.2
[08:10:01] kernel-selector: fallback to generic kernel (no optimized AVX path) due to cpu-sched hysteresis
```

tim_oncall: that kernel fallback line is interesting — it usually happens when CPU steal or scheduler latency crosses threshold. can we get perf counters and iostats from one host?

maria-ops: attached perf-bot snapshot from host ord-03 (collected at 08:12):
```
perf_top: sample period 2s
cpu: 75% user 12% sys 13% steal
top funcs: scheduler_tick, rq_lock, io_wait, memcpy
```
kstat: tx_errs spike on eth0 at same time, tx queue drops 42 -> 218

perf-bot: kvcache-miss-rate: +9.4% during window; batch-latency-50 -> 150ms; kernel-switch-count +220

alex_k: so network microbursts => tx drops => kernel scheduler sees backlog => kernel-selector flips to conservative kernel => batcher flushes early => throughput drops and kv warms -> more misses. feedback loop.

sasha: I can roll back the kernel-selector tweak for ORD to previous threshold and revert the batching window change on a couple canary hosts. want a controlled rollback first?

maria-ops: yes do canary 2 hosts, watch p95/p99 and kv-hit. coordinate with net team to validate peering.

tim_oncall: starting canary rollback now on ord-02 and ord-04 (rolling restart). will use tag rollback/ord/2660004321.

sasha: rolled back kernel-selector and batching window on ord-02. ord-02 p99 dropped from 780ms -> 210ms after restart, kv-hit recovered ~6%. ord-04 still restarting.

maria-ops: net team reports a short peering flap at 08:09-08:11 UTC between our peering edge and provider X (ticket PXR-9876). looks like transient network noise triggered the cascade.

alex_k: long-term we should harden the kernel-selector to avoid flipping on short-lived steal spikes and make batcher less likely to flush when kv-hit rate is high but RTT jitter spikes. Also add a short holdback (5s) before kernel fallback.

tim_oncall: opened follow-up task INF-4021: "ORD: add kernel-selector holdback + batcher resilience to peering microbursts". assigned to eng-runtime. ETA next sprint.

maria-ops: for now marking incident resolved. p99 back to normal for all hosts by 08:24 UTC. leaving the rollback in place until we ship a fix. :white_check_mark:

sasha: note for postmortem: include perf snapshots, kstat, and peering provider logs. we'll also add canary auto-rollback if kernel-selector flips >2x in 60s.

alex_k: thanks all. good catch correlating KV thrash with network microbursts — that coupling was subtle.

maria-ops: adding final notes to incident channel and will start a short postmortem doc.
